summary: The Affordable Health Care for America Act, also known as HR 3962, was a bill drafted by the United States House of Representatives on October 29, 2009. It did not become law in its original form. It was the House's main legislative proposal during the health reform debate that the 111th Congress spent much of its time on, at the encouragement of the Obama administration.
one_line: HR 3962, the 2009 House bill that served as the chief House proposal in the U.S. health care reform debate.
key_facts: The Affordable Health Care for America Act is also known as HR 3962.
The bill was crafted by the United States House of Representatives on October 29, 2009.
The bill never became law as originally drafted.
At the encouragement of the Obama administration, the 111th Congress devoted much of its time to enacting reform of the United States' health care system.
HR 3962 is known as the "House bill".
HR 3962 was the House of Representatives' chief legislative proposal during the health reform debate.
